verbalization: Dofequidar is implicated in the regulation of Phosphodiesterase 6C through multiple indirect pathways. The first pathway links Dofequidar to Branched-chain-amino-acid aminotransferase, cytosolic, which is targeted by 3,4-Dihydroxycinnamic Acid. This compound, in turn, has a target of Phosphodiesterase 6C, suggesting a potential regulatory cascade involving amino acid metabolism and enzyme activity. The second pathway reveals that Dofequidar targets Macrophage scavenger receptor types I and II, which is subsequently targeted by Islandicin 4-Methyl Ether, which also targets Phosphodiesterase 6C. These findings suggest that Dofequidar may influence Phosphodiesterase 6C through distinct but related mechanisms, possibly involving immune modulation and metabolic regulation. The integration of these pathways highlights the complex interplay between Dofequidar and Phosphodiesterase 6C, emphasizing the role of secondary metabolites in mediating this relationship.
